group_assessment.dominant_field: Corresponding/senior author Lu P-J (National Cheng Kung Univ, Tainan) has 472 PubMed records and only 3 on WWOX — this is a GSK3beta/prolyl-isomerase-and-cancer laboratory, not a WWOX laboratory. Decisive counterweight: co-author Chang N-S has 137 records of which 66 are on WWOX — he is the founder of the WWOX field. First author Wang H-Y has 2 WWOX records; Hsiao M has 1.
group_assessment.method: NCBI eutils esearch counts, 2026-07-26: 'Lu PJ[au]' 472; 'Lu PJ[au] AND WWOX' 3; 'Chang NS[au]' 137; 'Chang NS[au] AND WWOX' 66; 'Wang HY[au] AND WWOX' 2; 'Hsiao M[au] AND WWOX' 1. Author-name ambiguity is HIGH for these initial-form Taiwanese names; the counts bound magnitude, they do not identify individuals with certainty.
group_assessment.weighting: The two halves must be weighted separately and must not be merged. (1) The GSK3beta biochemistry — in-vitro kinase assay, GST pull-down domain mapping, point mutants, competitive peptide, microtubule light-scattering — is done by a group whose native expertise is kinase signalling. That is the part to trust most, and it is also the part that is internally self-consistent across five independent assay types. (2) The WWOX framing is backstopped by Chang N-S, the field's originator. That raises prior plausibility but imports a KNOWN dispute: PAPER 053 (Aldaz 2014) records that the Chang lab's WWOX localization and pro-apoptotic claims are contested, with Aldaz attributing part of them to adenoviral-vector artefact. Nothing in the present paper depends on that disputed localization, so the dispute does not propagate here — but any downstream use of this paper's WWOX cell-biology framing must carry the flag. (3) The reverse asymmetry of the Saadane case applies: here WWOX did NOT arrive through an unbiased screen; it was the starting hypothesis, supplied by the field's founder. The observation is therefore weaker as independent confirmation than a naive-lab hit would be, while the interpretation is stronger.
group_assessment.research_type_basis: Senior author Lu P-J runs a kinase-signalling lab (472 records, 3 on WWOX) — adjacent_method_expert for WWOX, experimental_lab for GSK3beta. Co-author Chang N-S is the founder of the WWOX field (66/137). Methods show a full wet-lab plus in-house MD capability: radiometric kinase assay, GST purification and domain mapping, site-directed mutagenesis, confocal, turbidimetric microtubule assay, CHARMM/Discovery Studio simulation. NOT a WOREE/disease group: no author works on the disease.

field_density.verdict: Five records in all of PubMed for WWOX x GSK3. In a rare disease a near-empty intersection means the edge is UNTESTED, not tested-and-rejected — the same reading applied to WWOX x calpain (2 records) in the PMID 34214506 manifest. Practical consequence: CLAIM 016 and the whole TX-005 lithium line currently rest on a two-paper literature, of which this is one. WWOX x DYRK1A returns ZERO, which is why the priming-kinase route proposed in the commit candidate is filed as IPOTESI/ESPANSIONE with no literature support whatsoever, not as an inference.

corpus_crossquery.verdict: This is NOT new territory — it is the opposite situation from the calpain case, and more uncomfortable. The residue L404 and the region 388-407 are ALREADY load-bearing in the analysis layer: therapeutic_strategies_current.md TX-003 and proteostasis_rationale.md both instruct that an SDR stabilizer 'must avoid the functional region (388-407/L404)', and the Q230P red-team report builds a whole 'second functional exclusion zone' on it. The red-team's own missing-info item 7 reads: 'Residue-level confirmation that L404 is required for WWOX-GSK3beta binding — cited (Wang et al., PMC3354054) but NOT VERIFIED here.' The paper was therefore CITED AS A PREMISE BY FIVE FILES WHILE UNREAD, and is absent from paper_registry_current.md. This deep dive exists to close that gap. Verdict: the premise holds — but the system had been running on an unverified citation.
